Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

You ever wake up with your footie PJs warming your neck like a noose? Ever upchuck after a home-cooked meal? Or notice how the blood on the bottoms of your feet just won’t seem to go away? Love, it used to be you could retire your toothbrush for like two or three days and still I’d push my downy face into your neck. Used to be I hung on your every word. (Sing! you’d say: and I was a bird.Freedom! you’d say: and I never really knew what that meant, but liked the way it rang like a rusty bell.) Used to be. But now I can tell you your breath stinks and you’re full of shit. You have more lies about yourself than bodies beneath your bed. Rootingfor the underdog. Team player. Hook, line and sinker. Love, you helped design the brick that built the walls around the castle in the basement of which is a vault inside of which is another vault inside of which . . . you get my point. Your tongue is made of honey but flicks like a snake’s. Voice like a bird but everyone’s ears are bleeding. From the inside your house shines and shines, but from outside you can see it’s built from bones. From out here it looks like a graveyard, and the garden’s all ash. And besides, your breath stinks. We’re through.

outputs.L1:
Here are two ways to polish the text, depending on the tone you wish to achieve:

### Option 1: Literary & Poetic Eloquence (Recommended)
*This version elevates the text into dramatic, high-level prose while maintaining all the dark, vivid imagery and emotional impact of the original monologue.*

> "Have you ever awakened to find your softest garments constricting your neck like a noose? Have you ever felt nauseated after a home-cooked meal, or noticed that the blood staining the soles of your feet simply refuses to wash away? 
> 
> My love, there was a time when you could neglect yourself for days, and I would still press my face softly into your neck. There was a time when I hung on your every word. When you commanded me to sing, I became a songbird; when you spoke of freedom, I embraced the idea without truly understanding it, simply enchanted by how the word resonated like a weathered bell. 
> 
> That, however, was then. Now, I can tell you plainly that your words are foul and your nature is thoroughly deceitful. You harbor more false narratives about yourself than hidden sins beneath your bed. Champion of the underdog, dedicated team player—illusions accepted hook, line, and sinker. 
> 
> My love, you helped craft the very bricks that built the walls of a fortress, beneath which lies a basement concealing vault after vault... but you understand my point. Your tongue drips with honey, yet it strikes like a serpent’s. Your voice mimics a bird’s song, yet it leaves the ears of those who listen bleeding from within. From the inside, your house appears radiant and pristine; from out here, however, it is clearly constructed from bones. From this vantage point, it resembles a graveyard, and the garden is reduced to ash. 
> 
> And besides, your breath remains foul. We are finished."

***

### Option 2: Refined & Sophisticated
*This version softens the visceral crude terms into elegant, sharp critiques, suitable for a refined dramatic piece.*

> "Have you ever woken up feeling suffocated by your own comfort, as though it were a tight loop around your neck? Have you ever been sickened by a meal prepared at home, or realized that the blood on the bottoms of your feet will never wash clean? 
> 
> My dear, there was a time when you could go days without basic care, and I would still press my face close to yours. I used to hang on your every word. If you bade me to sing, I sang like a bird. If you spoke of freedom, I accepted it blindly, captivated merely by the resonant sound of the word. That was in the past. 
> 
> Now, I can be honest: your breath is repulsive, and you are entirely disingenuous. You possess more self-serving fabrications than buried secrets. A champion of the underdog, a loyal team player—a charade swallowed hook, line, and sinker. 
> 
> My love, you helped design the very bricks forming the fortress walls, inside of which is a basement, containing a vault within a vault... but you grasp my meaning. Your tongue is sweet as honey, yet it flicks like a serpent's. Your voice sounds like a songbird, yet it leaves everyone’s ears bleeding from the inside. From within, your home shines brilliantly, but from the outside, it is visibly built of bones. From out here, it is nothing more than a graveyard with a garden of ash. 
> 
> Furthermore, your breath is foul. We are done."
outputs.L2:
Do you know the feeling of opening your eyes to find your cozy sleepwear suffocating your throat? Have you ever thrown up right after eating a meal prepared at home? Or observed how the blood staining the undersides of your feet refuses to wash away? 

Darling, there was a time when you could neglect your oral hygiene for several days, and I would still press my soft face against your skin. Back then, I hung on every single thing you said. When you told me to sing, I warbled like a bird; when you spoke of liberty, I adored the metallic chime of the word, even without grasping its true meaning. That was the past. 

Now, I am free to inform you that your breath is foul and your character is utterly deceitful. You hoard more fabrications about your own virtue than hidden corpses beneath your mattress. You completely fell for your own narrative of being a supportive collaborator who champions the vulnerable. In truth, my love, you assisted in crafting the very bricks that constructed the fortress, deep beneath which lies an endless chain of locked safes inside locked safes. 

Your speech is coated in sweetness yet strikes like a serpent. Your tone sounds melodious, yet it makes the ears of your audience hemorrhage. From your perspective indoors, your residence gleams brightly, but looking at it from the outside, it is clearly constructed from human remains. From this vantage point, it appears as a tomb surrounded by a yard of cinder. 

Ultimately, your breath is repulsive, and our relationship is finished.
outputs.L3:
There was a time when my devotion to you was absolute—a quiet, unshakeable allegiance born of deep affection and trust. Today, however, that obedience has withered into nothingness. Looking back, I realize that my love was never truly anchored in who you are, but in a carefully crafted illusion I was led to believe. The veil has finally fallen, and with it, every remaining trace of warmth I once felt for you has dissolved.

To the outside world, you present an immaculate portrait of virtue, humility, and selflessness. You wear your moral superiority like a well-tailored garment, easily earning the admiration of those who only see the surface. But beneath this meticulously curated public persona lies a deeply dishonest nature—a cold, calculating reality that stands in stark contrast to the noble image you project to everyone else.

What is most unforgivable is not merely the deceit, but the deliberate calculation behind it. Brick by brick, you helped build a suffocating, multi-layered trap designed with one ultimate purpose: to isolate me. Every subtle manipulation, every quiet effort to distance me from support and independence, was part of a conscious strategy to narrow my world until you were the only authority left within it.

It is a tragic paradox. You possess a charm that is undeniably captivating, an alluring facade capable of disarming almost anyone. Yet, beneath that beautiful surface lies an existence that is fundamentally destructive. Like a sweet poison, your presence does not nurture; it slowly erodes everything authentic, healthy, and whole in its path.

I will no longer remain silent, nor will I continue to bear the weight of your hypocrisy. Having fully confronted the toxic truth of who you are and what you have done, I am reclaiming my freedom. The illusion is shattered, the trap is broken, and this relationship is officially and irrevocably over.
outputs.L4:
For months, I mistook your gilded tongue for sunlight. I drank in your promises like desperate soil welcoming a monsoon, kneeling at an altar built entirely of paper and smoke. Back then, my devotion was absolute—a blind, trembling thing that mistook your possessiveness for passion and your calculated silences for depth. I poured myself into the cracks of your moodiness, believing that if I loved you gently enough, I could soothe whatever quiet war you claimed was raging in your soul.

I know better now. The scales haven't merely fallen from my eyes; they have been scraped away by the jagged reality of who you truly are. 

You are an architect of subtle violence. Your charm was never warmth—it was a velvet sheath designed to hide a blade that cut me every time I leaned in close. To watch you operate is to watch a master weaver spin silk out of poison. You knew precisely which soft parts of my past to target, twisting my vulnerabilities into handles you could use to pull me wherever you wished. Every sweet gesture was a transaction; every apology, a loan with exorbitant interest designed to keep me bankrupt and dependent. 

My stomach churns when I look back at the sheer scale of my own naivety. How sickeningly easy it was for you to smile while bleeding me dry. You wrapped your cruelty in the language of concern, making me question my own memory, my own sanity, until I was apologizing for the bruising your words left behind. The realization didn't hit me like a sudden lightning strike, but like the slow, terrifying spread of rot. I began to see the rust beneath your polish, the cold, calculating eye that watched me break and felt only the quiet thrill of ownership.

The illusion hasn't just shattered; it has decomposed. I look at you today and see no lingering beauty, only the hollow shell of a predator who mistook my tenderness for weakness. 

Consider this the final bill for your feast, because I am no longer on the menu. I am pulling out the threads of you that I allowed to weave into my skin, no matter how much it burns to tear them free. I will not weep for the man I thought you were, because he was nothing more than a ghost you constructed to trap me. You can keep your curated charm, your practiced vulnerability, and your endless, suffocating games. I am severing this tether. I am walking away, leaving you alone in the dark house of mirrors you built for us both, with only your own reflection left to consume you.
outputs.L5:
There is a specific kind of magic that belongs entirely to Sunday mornings. The world outside is constantly rushing, chasing deadlines and carefully curated appearances, but inside these four walls, time seems to pause just for us. 

I watch **you** walk into the kitchen, rubbing the sleep from your eyes, bathed in the soft morning light filtering through the blinds. You’re wearing those oversized flannel **PJs**—the ones that are a little too long at the sleeves and washed so many times they’ve become impossibly soft. There’s no pretense here, no makeup, no armor against the world. It’s just you, entirely relaxed, holding a warm mug of coffee with both hands.

People often talk about love in terms of grand gestures—fancy dinners, dressed-up dates, and memorable trips. But standing here, watching you lean against the counter in your favorite pajamas, I realize that this quiet intimacy is the best thing **ever**. It’s in these unscheduled, unscripted moments that I feel closest to you. 

Out of all the versions of you I’ve grown to love over the years, this cozy, unfiltered version will always be my absolute favorite.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a dark, poetic monologue for an acting audition where a character venomously breaks up with a partner who turned out to be a deceitful hypocrite. Use vivid, grotesque imagery contrasting former devotion with current disgust.
counterfactuals.output:
**(Stage Directions: The character begins with a quiet, terrifying calm, almost a whisper. As the monologue progresses, the facade of control cracks, revealing visceral, venomous disgust.)**

**(A slow, quiet laugh, devoid of humor)**

Don’t pray for me now. Please. Keep your lily-white hands folded—you wouldn’t want to smudge the paint. 

Do you remember how I used to look at you? I used to drink the air you breathed like it was holy water. I built a sanctuary inside my own chest, stripped my own skin just to line the walls with gold for you. I thought you were porcelain. I thought you were pure, unblemished light. I knelt at your altar every night, blind to the damp… utterly blind to the black mold crawling up the wood.

*(A sharp beat. The voice hardens into steel.)*

But you aren't porcelain, are you? You’re just cheap plaster, hollowed out and stuffed with rot. 

How long have you been decaying behind that saintly smile? Tell me. When you kissed me this morning, did you feel it? The sudden, violent urge to vomit? Because I did. The moment your lips touched mine, I didn't taste sweet devotion anymore. I tasted bile. I tasted the sulfur of every pious lie you’ve ever choked up while parading yourself as a martyr. 

*(Stepping closer, voice dropping to a harsh, lethal venom)*

You preach about purity while you crawl through the filth on your belly, dragging your little secret sins behind you like a swollen, maggot-ridden tail. And the most grotesque part—the absolute *funniest* part—is that you still believe your own sermon. You sit there, wrapped in your self-righteous robes, completely oblivious to the fact that you reek of carrion. 

I’m not crying because my heart is broken. Look at me. I’m crying because my body is trying to purge you. I am gagging on the memory of loving you. 

Keep your pathetic, trembling apologies. Keep your god. I am scraping your name off my tongue, tearing you out of my veins, every sickening, parasitic inch of you. I am burning the sanctuary to the ground… and I am locking you inside. 

Get out of my sight. Before I throw up on your shoes.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a surreal, bitter breakup speech using dark domestic imagery (footie PJs, bad breath, houses made of bones).
counterfactuals.output:
Look at this place, darling. Really look at it. 

We thought we were building a home, but all we did was stack our old skeletons, interlocking the phalanges to keep the cold out. Look up—the ceiling is just a lattice of our own yellowed ribcages, and every time the wind blows, the attic rattles like a dead man’s dice. The floorboards are leaking marrow again. I told you three months ago to call a plumber, but you were too busy sitting on the couch, watching the white noise on the TV, unspooling your own intestines like yarn.

Sit down. Stop picking at your nails. 

You’re sitting there in those fleece, footie PJs—the ones with the faded little stars—looking like a giant, overgrown fetus trapped in a synthetic body bag. You think it’s cute. You think the static electricity you generate when you drag your feet across the carpet is a spark. It’s not a spark. It’s just cheap friction. It’s the sound of synthetic fabric slowly suffocating the last decent piece of flesh you have left. 

And please, for the love of God, don’t open your mouth to explain yourself. 

Your breath comes out of you like a basement door being opened after a flood. It smells like stale instant coffee, swallowed resentment, and small, warm-blooded things that died behind the refrigerator three winters ago and were simply left to petrify. Every time you lean in to kiss me goodnight, I feel the spores landing on my tongue. You exhale rust into my throat and expect me to call it warmth. I’ve spent five years brushing my teeth until my gums bled, trying to scrub the taste of your morning apologies off my palate.

I’m done swimming through the grease of this routine. I’m done scraping your dry skin out of the bedsheets. 

Yesterday, I tried to make us breakfast, but when I opened the butter dish, there were just six of your baby teeth resting on the porcelain. You didn’t even notice. You just poured hot vinegar into the kettle, smiled through your grey, furred tongue, and told me to drink my tea before it got cold.

I am leaving. 

No, don't get up. Don't waddle toward me in your soft, padded feet. You'll trip over the femur holding up the front door. 

Stay right there in your quiet, rotting little nursery. Zip your footie PJs all the way up over your mouth, pull the hood down over your eyes, and stew in the warm, damp air of your own lungs. The bone rafters are sagging, darling. The spine of this hallway is finally going to snap. And when the house comes down around you, crunching like a dry beetle under a heel, don’t bother calling my name. 

It already rotted out of your mouth a long time ago, and I am not coming back to dig you out of the ribs.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you draft a monologue from the perspective of someone who used to worship their lover like a bird obeying a call, but now sees through their lies, vault-like secrets, and toxic behavior? End it with "We’re through."
counterfactuals.output:
Do you remember how I used to look at you? 

Whenever you spoke, it was like a call carried on the wind—pure, magnetic, undeniable. I was like a bird wired entirely to your frequency. You whistled, and I flew. It didn't matter how dark the sky was, how tired my wings were, or how much of myself I had to leave behind; if you called, I dropped out of the air just to land at your feet. I thought you were my sky. I thought you were teaching me how to soar.

But you weren't a sky at all, were you? You were a cage. 

I was so blinded by the glare of your ego that I couldn't see the cold metal around me. All those times you claimed you were "private"? You weren't guarded, you were a vault. A heavy, airless vault filled with double lives, buried truths, and quiet, calculated lies. And every time I tried to reach for the real you, every time I asked for simple honesty, you turned it into a crime. You made me feel insane for noticing the chill in the room. You fed on my devotion while dripping venom into my ear, convincing me that your toxicity was just "passion," that your control was just "protection."

I muted my own song just so yours could be the only sound in the world. I cut off my own instincts to obey yours.

Well, look at me now. Look at me really looking at you. 

The spell is broken. The vault door opened, and I finally saw what you’ve been hiding behind all that steel: a small, hollow person who only feels big when someone else is on their knees. 

So go ahead. Call out. Whistle for me. Try that old spell one more time and see what happens. 

I’m not listening anymore. I'm spreading my wings, and I am taking my sky back. 

We’re through.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a piece of visceral flash fiction about falling out of love with a covert manipulator. Make the tone raw, angry, and slightly unhinged.
counterfactuals.output:
He used his sad voice. The one he pulled out like a tarnished spoon whenever I dared to exist at a volume higher than a whisper. 

*“I’m just worried about you,”* he said, tilting his head with that exquisite, practiced sorrow. *“You get so defensive when you’re unstable.”*

And just like that, the lock clicked. The spell didn't break—it ruptured. 

It didn't happen like a candle blowing out. It happened like a pipe bursting in the wall, spewing black sewage all over the polished marble of my devotion. The love didn't fade; it rotted sideways, bursting through my ribs like a hot, greasy boil. 

I looked at his face. Really looked at it. Not the tragic-martyr portrait he’d spent three years painting for me, but the sniveling, thumb-sized man beneath it. The grease on his nose. The faint, satisfied twitch at the corner of his mouth because he thought I was about to apologize. He *always* thought I was about to apologize. He built a little palace out of my shame and sat in it like a king made of soft butter.

*You get so defensive.* 

God, it was breathtaking. It was a masterpiece of bloodless violence. He didn't punch; he just bled on me until I felt guilty for holding the knife he’d shoved into his own chest.

A warm, wet bubble of laughter hissed up my throat. It tasted like copper and vinegar. 

"What's funny?" he asked, his voice dropping half an octave, setting the trap. *Step into the net, honey. Tell me I'm a monster so I can cry and make you feed me soup.*

I squeezed my fork so hard my knuckles went the color of lard. My teeth clicked together, grinding down the urge to scream until my jaws squeaked. I wanted to peel my own skin off just to scrub the grease of his approval off the back of my neck. Every "I'm sorry" I had ever given him swelled up in my belly like swallowed sponges, expanding, dry and choking, suffocating me with all the apologies I’d wasted on a ghost.

"You're not sad," I wheezed. My voice sounded flat. Cracked. Beautifully ruined.

"Excuse me?" He shrank back, pulling his shoulders in, setting the stage to play the abused dog. *Look at her, everyone. Look how mean she is to me.*

"You're not sad," I snapped, leaning across the table until I could smell the stale coffee on his breath. "You're a parasite in a wool sweater. You’re a little gray slug drowning in your own salt."

"You're having an episode," he whispered, weaponizing his pity like a velvet sap. "Let me help you."

I laughed out loud this time. It was an ugly, barking noise that startled a woman three tables over. It felt *glare-bright*. It felt unhinged. 

I leaned closer, feeling the magnificent, terrifying snap of my sanity settling into its true socket. 

"If I hear you fake a sigh one more time," I whispered, my eyes burning wide, "I am going to swallow these cloth napkins whole, spit them onto your shoes, and watch you try to apologize for the mess."

His eyes flickered. Just for a microsecond. The saint mask slipped, and underneath was just a blank, furious boy who had run out of tricks. 

I didn't pack. I didn't cry. I just stood up, threw my glass of ice water directly into my own lap to feel something cold, and walked out into the rain, laughing so hard my lungs felt like cut glass.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Give me a speech dumping a hypocritical ex.
counterfactuals.output:
Here is a direct, powerful speech designed to call out the hypocrisy, reclaim your power, and end the relationship cleanly. 

***

"We need to stop pretending this is working, because I am completely done. 

I’ve spent a lot of time giving you the benefit of the doubt, but I’ve finally realized what this relationship actually is: a massive double standard. You hold me to perfection while you slide by on excuses. You preach about honesty, communication, and respect, but the moment the spotlight is on *your* behavior, those rules suddenly don't apply. 

It’s rules for me, and excuses for you. 

If I acted the way you act, you’d call me toxic. You’d call me selfish. But when *you* do it, there’s always a reason, a justification, or a way to twist it so that somehow *I’m* the one apologizing. You love to play the saint and the victim, but you never take accountability for being the problem. 

I used to think you had high standards. Now I see it for what it is: self-righteousness. You love the *idea* of being a good partner, but you don't actually want to do the work of being one. You just want someone you can critique so you don't have to look at your own flaws.

I’m not playing this game anymore. I’m not going to spend my energy meeting expectations that you can’t even touch. 

Don't bother trying to explain it away, and please don't pull out the script of promises you have no intention of keeping. The illusion is gone. I deserve someone whose actions actually match their words—and that is clearly not you. 

We are done. Do not call me, do not text me, and please do not pretend to be confused about why this is happening. Goodbye."

***

### 💡 Tips for Delivery:
* **Keep your voice level:** Hypocrites thrive on turning your anger into "proof" that *you* are the crazy one. Delivering this calmly, coldly, and with complete certainty takes away their power to manipulate the narrative.
* **Don't debate:** Once you finish speaking, **walk away or hang up**. A hypocrite will immediately try to point out *your* flaws to shift the focus back onto you. Do not give them an audience.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
